hey <@U0004>, <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/issues/4193|#4193> is the warning budget you floated when <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/issues/612|#612> closed. It covers two packages for now, not the whole repo.

It differs from your sketch in one way. Each package's count lives in `.baselines/` and can only go down, instead of being worked out from the diff on every run. That means it counts the whole package, and git blame shows every drop.

Tell me if you disagree. A drop fails until it is recorded, so a PR that only removes old code also runs one rebaseline command. I want that friction; without it the count creeps up and stops meaning anything. Making it silent is a two-line change if you prefer that.

The description has a recording of all three cases.

messages.author: UOWNER
messages.authoredText: Our style guide lists rules that no tool enforces. It says new code adds no untyped values, yet the matching lint rule is a warning in one package of nine, which is how <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/3911|#3911> slipped in. Idea: every rule a tool can decide becomes a check, and the guide keeps the reason. What always stops that is the existing backlog, since a check that fails in 840 places cannot simply be switched on. So: a ratchet. Record the count, fail on any rise, accept any fall. No mass rewrite and no regressions. <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4193|#4193> shows it working; .baselines/ can hold any countable defect, not only this one. Which guide rules would you want turned into checks, and which should stay a matter of judgement?

messages.author: UOWNER
messages.authoredText: hey, our style guide lists rules nothing enforces. Turning them into checks is the obvious move, but a check that fails in hundreds of places needs one huge cleanup PR before it can go on: a wide blast radius, and nobody wants to touch the area afterwards. Grace, Barbara and I hit exactly this with unused exports. So: a ratchet. The check lands as a warning, its repo-wide count is committed, and CI fails when the count rises. Flat or falling is fine. The backlog stays exempt but cannot grow, and it shrinks PR by PR rather than all at once. <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4193|#4193> shows it on the untyped-values rule, though that rule is only the example. One catch: the count does not update itself. When a PR lowers it you run one command and commit a one-line change. Which guide rules would you turn into a ratcheted check first?

messages.author: UOWNER
messages.authoredText: hey, our style guide lists rules nothing enforces. Turning them into checks is the obvious move, but a check that fails in hundreds of places needs one huge cleanup PR before it can go on: a wide blast radius, and nobody wants to touch the area afterwards. Grace, Barbara and I hit exactly this with unused exports. So: a ratchet, run inside the lint step we already have. The check is an error everywhere. Each package commits its current count, and only that many are let through. One more fails CI and the commit. One fewer rewrites the count in the pre-commit hook, so nobody runs anything and the number only goes down. <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4193|#4193> is the mechanism alone, with today's counts and no fixes. A second PR on top of it clears the worst package and records the first fall. The untyped-values rule is just the example.

messages.authoredText:
<@U0014> <@U0012> bringing this one to you as a product call rather than a code review.

<https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4231|#4231> stops the editor dropping someone on the home page when their draft saves but the session refresh after it fails. Instead they now land on the generic error screen. Thaddeus pointed out that screen is wrong for this case: it says "Something went wrong" with a button back into an empty editor, which suggests the draft was lost when it was kept, and "Please log in to continue" with no way to log in.

Two options and I'm not sure enough to pick between them.

1. Send the fallback to `/login` carrying `redirect`, the way the signed-out branch already does.

2. Give `SaveError` a saved-but-signed-out variant: no empty-editor button, a login button, and copy that says the draft was kept.

This path comes up often enough that it is worth settling. Both editors share it, so whatever we pick lands twice.

Why I want your answer before building it: there's no point lining the tests up with the current behaviour if the current behaviour isn't what we want.

Thaddeus's two comments: <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4231#discussion_r[number]|the detailed one> and <https://github.com/acme/acme-admin/pull/4231#discussion_r[number]|the same issue in the other editor>. The other five threads on the PR are fixed and resolved; this is the only thing left. Parked until one of you decides.
